label: Gatterer Synopsis colour has an established cognitive/visual-method historiography

observations.value: Araújo treats Gatterer's synchronistic tables as part of a new scientific visual semantics and analyzes hand-applied colour as a means of highlighting boundaries and major historical revolutions while surviving copies diverge in pigment state.

sources.citation: André de Melo Araújo, Imagens da simultaneidade e os impasses da narrativa: O caso da Synopsis historiae universalis (1766) de Johann Christoph Gatterer, Tempo 21.38 (2015): 192-215

claim_limit: Do not claim novelty merely for identifying cognitive use of colour in the Synopsis. The open problem is how this colour regime relates to other historical colour regimes and to copy invariance.

label: Eighteenth-century colour charts and reference systems now have an integrated historiography

observations.value: Simonini integrates natural, pigmentary and trichromatic colour charts and reconstructs eighteenth-century problems of colour terminology, samples, standardization, material practice and systematic order.

sources.citation: Giulia Simonini, Color Charts in 18th-century Europe: Natural, Pigmentary, Trichromatic (Heidelberg, 2025)

claim_limit: Do not claim novelty for eighteenth-century colour standardization/order. Test separately whether monochrome heraldic chromatic decoders belong to or fall outside this sample-centered chart historiography.

label: Scientific hand-colouring already has a methodological history

observations.value: Nickelsen reconstructs supervision, evaluation, recipes, standardization and reproducibility problems in eighteenth-century hand-coloured botanical illustration, including Nuremberg-based Trew and colour-reference systems.

sources.citation: Kärin Nickelsen, The Challenge of Colour: Eighteenth-Century Botanists and the Hand-Colouring of Illustrations, Annals of Science 63.1 (2006): 3-23

claim_limit: Do not claim novelty for copy variance, recipe instability or methodological difficulty of hand-colouring as such.

label: Göttingen was already an active site of eighteenth-century colour science

observations.value: Scholarship identifies Tobias Mayer, Erxleben and Lichtenberg as important Göttingen actors in eighteenth-century colour science, including early trichromatic thinking.

sources.citation: Barry B. Lee, Colour science in Göttingen in the 18th Century, Color Research & Application 26 (2001)

claim_limit: Institutional coexistence is context only. No influence on Gatterer's historical colour practice is established without direct contact evidence.

label: Secondary scholarship identifies colour as a classificatory dimension in Gatterer's 1775 Menschen- und Völkerkunde

observations.value: Gatterer's Abriß der Geographie is reconstructed as beginning Menschen- und Völkerkunde with a geography of human bodies by shape and colour, placing colour in a classificatory rather than representational role.

sources.citation: Modern reconstruction of Gatterer's 1775 geography classification, reporting Geography of human bodies, by shape and colour as the first Menschen- und Völkerkunde chapter

claim_limit: Primary Gatterer wording must be inspected before promotion. Do not merge this with later racial typologies or with heraldic/synchronistic colour regimes.

label: Working gap: colour translation regimes as historical method

observations.value: The first sweep has not identified a study that follows colour across connected historical and auxiliary-historical practices as a sequence of translation regimes: verbal colour, letter code, hatching, centralized monochrome decoder, copy-level pigment, abstract relational syntax and classificatory description, while tracking how each regime redistributes reproducibility, inspectability, fidelity and error.

claim_limit: Bounded negative historiographical claim. Reopen if directly overlapping work on heraldic chromatic notation, historical tables, Göttingen historical colour method or cross-domain colour translation is identified.

label: Working gap: the monochrome chromatic decoder

observations.value: The Wappenkalender Erklärung der Farben functions as a reproducible monochrome decoder linking hatch signs, semantic tinctures and multilingual colour names. It differs materially from sample-based natural/pigmentary colour charts because no actual red, blue or green sample is required on the page.

sources.citation: Giulia Simonini, Color Charts in 18th-century Europe (2025)

claim_limit: Do not assert absence from the full colour-chart literature until targeted searches for heraldic hatching/tincture keys are completed.
